```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(yieldlag)
```

## Model family

Let $y_{it}$ be yield in region $i$ and harvest year $t$, and $x_{it}$ the
declared monthly weather vector. Available methods are:

- `trend`: independent linear trend in each region;
- `persistence`: the most recent observed yield in each region, providing a
  hard-to-beat operational baseline;
- `panel_ridge`: shared weather effects with regularized region intercepts and
  trends;
- `local_ridge`: separate regularized weather response in each region;
- `pcr`: training-window principal-component regression plus region effects;
- `hierarchical`: a global distributed-lag response with regularized regional
  deviations;
- `stress_lag`: asymmetric weather anomalies and optional matched-month hot-dry interactions;
- `ensemble`: non-negative, sum-to-one stacking of requested base methods.

Ridge penalties address the short time series relative to monthly terms.
Optional second-difference penalties smooth consecutive monthly coefficients.
Supported models use Student-t-style iteratively reweighted fitting and a
bounded pooled AR(1) correction based only on preceding residuals.

## Validation contract

Years are split chronologically into:

1. initial history;
2. rolling-origin tuning and interval calibration;
3. later rolling-origin evaluation.

For a prediction in year $t$, scaling, decomposition, fitting, and residual
correction use yields strictly before $t$. Hyperparameters are chosen on the
tuning block. Ensemble shrinkage is chosen by holding out one complete tuning
year at a time. Automatic method selection minimizes province-year tuning
RMSE; later evaluation is not used for selection.

The 80% province interval is the 80th percentile of absolute tuning errors.
National intervals are recalibrated from national tuning errors because
averaging province intervals would ignore spatial correlation.

## Interpretation limits

Province-year rows share years and regions and are not independent replicates.
National evaluation often contains very few years. Predictive R-squared may be
negative and should not be replaced by squared correlation. Once an evaluation
block has influenced development, a new later or external dataset is required
for a confirmatory claim.

The package exposes all row-level predictions so users can add blocked
bootstrap uncertainty, spatial holdouts, and crop-specific diagnostics rather
than relying only on aggregate scores.

## Nonlinear seasonal response

The stress-lag estimator constructs z = (x - regional monthly mean) / pooled
within-region standard deviation inside each training window. Its basis contains
z, max(z - tau, 0), and max(-z - tau, 0). Explicit temperature/precipitation
labels enable products of upper-temperature and lower-precipitation anomalies
at matching months. Dimensionless tau is tuned with ridge/smoothing strengths.

Penalties smooth monthly coefficients separately for each variable/basis component.
Decompositions reproduce the fitted equation; marginal range diagnostics flag
weather beyond training support. These are statistical diagnostics. Nonlinear
exposure responses and distributed-lag models are established methods (Schlenker
and Roberts, 2009, doi:10.1073/pnas.0906865106; Gasparrini et al., 2010,
doi:10.1002/sim.3940). YieldLag uses a penalized seasonal hinge/product basis,
rather than daily heat exposure or the full distributed-lag cross-basis formulation.
